paper.title: Does 1/2-Tsallis-INF Also Work Well for Best-Arm Identification?

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-armed bandit; failure probability Err_t of the empirical best arm from importance-weighted cumulative loss estimates
unmapped: Error probability is evaluated at every time t (anytime) for a regret-minimizing algorithm without a stopping/budget input; the recommendation is the argmin of cumulative importance-weighted loss estimates
Loss vectors (not only marginals) are i.i.d. from a joint distribution D on [0,1]^d
settings.definition_quote: We study a stochastic multi-armed bandit problem with arm set $\mathcal{I}=\{1,\ldots,d\}$. ... the environment produces a loss vector $\ell_t\in[0,1]^d$. The learner only observes and suffers the loss $\ell_{t,I_t}$ of the chosen arm. ... loss vectors are i.i.d. draws from an unknown distribution $\mathcal{D}$. ... $i_*$ the unique optimal arm ... We study the failure probability $\Err_t=\P(i_{t}^*\ne i_*)$.

algorithms.name: 1/2-Tsallis-INF (FTRL with -4 sum sqrt(p_i), eta_t = alpha/sqrt(t), IW estimators)

symbols.q: polynomial decay exponent, q = 2 - alpha_lr^2 mu_istar/4 - rho with rho > 0
symbols.mu_istar: mean loss of the optimal arm
symbols.C_aqr: constant depending only on alpha_lr, q and rho

source.label: et
source.quote: For Algorithm \ref{alg: FTRL}, if $i_*$ is unique and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, then for any $t\ge 1$ and $q\in(0,2-\frac{\alpha^2 \mu_{i_*}}{4})$, there exists $C_{\alpha,q,\rho}>0$ depending only on $\alpha$, $q$ and $\rho:=2-\frac{\alpha^2 \mu_{i_*}}{4}-q$ such that \[ \Err_t\leq C_{\alpha,q,\rho}\frac{d^{3q}(\log(d))^{2q}}{\Delta^{4q}}t^{-q}. \]

results.notes: Paper's d = number of arms (K); Delta = smallest positive gap (Delta_min); t is the current round (T). Err_t is a probability of misidentification at time t. Constant unspecified so notation O.

bound.regime: t >= C (constant independent of t), any eps_alg > 0

conditions: applies only to the specific algorithm 1/2-Tsallis-INF (Algorithm 1) with eta_t = alpha/sqrt(t), 0<alpha<1
mean loss of the optimal arm mu_{i_*} > 0

source.label: lower
source.quote: For Algorithm \ref{alg: FTRL}, if $i_*$ is unique, $\mu_{i_*}>0$ and $0<\alpha<1$, then for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $C $ and $C'>0$ that are independent of $t$ such that for any $t\ge C$, we have \[ \Err_t\ge C' t^{-2-\varepsilon}. \]

results.notes: Algorithm-specific lower bound (not minimax over algorithms). Constants C, C' depend on d, Delta, eps in an unspecified way.
